Based on the error log, the compiler is failing on the `ZTEST_SUITE` macro definition in `subsys/testsuite/ztest/include/zephyr/ztest_test.h`. The error "initializer element is not constant" for the `.stats` field, combined with the "expected declaration or statement at end of input" error, suggests a syntax issue that is confusing the compiler.

Comparing `ZTEST_SUITE` with similar macros like `Z_TEST` and `Z_TEST_P` in the same file reveals a subtle difference: `ZTEST_SUITE` has a trailing comma after the last element in its struct initializer list, while the others do not. While trailing commas are allowed in C99, some compilers can be stricter or have bugs related to them, especially within complex macro expansions.

Removing the trailing comma makes the `ZTEST_SUITE` macro consistent with other macros in `ztest_test.h` and is likely to resolve the compilation errors.

Here is the fix:

<subsys/testsuite/ztest/include/zephyr/ztest_test.h>
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
		.predicate = PREDICATE,                                                            \
		.stats = &UTIL_CAT(z_ztest_suite_node_stats_, SUITE_NAME),             \
	}
========
		.predicate = PREDICATE,                                                            \
		.stats = &UTIL_CAT(z_ztest_suite_node_stats_, SUITE_NAME)                          \
	}
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
